stemBlocks.value: In triangle OAB, OA = r and OB = s. E is the midpoint of CD, OC = (3/4)OA and AD = (2/3)AB. Write, in terms of r and s in simplest form, an expression for (i) CD and (ii) OE.
Think first: C is on OA and D is on AB, so find the position vector of each before attempting CD.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p287-q10 from workbook page 287.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the position vector of C using OC = (3/4)OA.
Find AB, then AD as two-thirds of it, and add to OA to reach D.
Subtract OC from OD to get CD.
Use the midpoint rule on C and D to find OE.

strategyBlocks.value: Write OC = (3/4)r, find AB then take two-thirds of it to locate D, subtract to get CD, and average OC and OD to get OE.

whyThisWorks.value: Taking O as origin means every named point has a position vector, and a vector between two points is always the difference of their position vectors. The fractions OC = (3/4)OA and AD = (2/3)AB place C and D exactly, and once both are in terms of r and s the subtraction is pure algebra. A midpoint is the average of the two ends, so OE follows immediately without needing to travel through C.

commonErrors.misconception: Using AD = (2/3)OB instead of (2/3)AB — the fraction is of AB, not of a side from O.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using AD = (2/3)OB instead of (2/3)AB — the fraction is of AB, not of a side from O.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing OD = (2/3)(s − r) and forgetting to add OA.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing OD = (2/3)(s − r) and forgetting to add OA.

commonErrors.misconception: Careless fraction work: 1/3 − 3/4 is −5/12, not 5/12 or −2/12.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Careless fraction work: 1/3 − 3/4 is −5/12, not 5/12 or −2/12.

commonErrors.misconception: Taking OE as half of CD rather than the average of OC and OD.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Taking OE as half of CD rather than the average of OC and OD.

examTip.value: Convert every ratio or fraction into a position vector from the origin as soon as you read it; the rest of the question then becomes subtraction.
